title: Egress Observability + NAT Debugging Runbook
content:
Purpose:
This runbook documents pragmatic steps for diagnosing and remediating egress-related failures in Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), with a focus on NAT, split-horizon DNS interactions, firewall rules, and telemetry required to make root-cause analysis fast. It includes proposed Terraform module adjustments, observability dashboards/alerts, and a safe upgrade/cutover plan for migrating from per-zone SNAT to a centralized egress gateway.

Scope / assumptions:
- Applies to private-deployments (VPC and on-prem) shipped via the Private control plane.
- Target stacks: GCP VPC + Cloud NAT hybrid, AWS VPC + NAT Gateway, and on-prem appliance NAT (via F5/HAProxy NAT boxes).
- We assume customers may have split-horizon DNS (internal zones pointing to internal endpoints) and DNS overrides that affect egress selection.
- This runbook focuses on networking and infra-level fixes; app-layer retries remain recommended.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Are customer pods/instances seeing DNS failures or timeouts? Check resolver latencies (node-local-dns metrics) and /etc/resolv.conf.
2) Confirm whether failures are to PRIVATE or PUBLIC destinations. Use tcpdump/pscap on node or host NAT to inspect SNI/IPs.
3) Verify source IP observed by destinations (if reachable) to confirm SNAT behavior.
4) Check NAT pool exhaustion: review active connections per NAT IP vs pool size.
5) Inspect firewall logs for DROP/REJECT on egress ports (80/443 and any configured service ports).
6) Look for recent terraform/apply runs that touched egress modules (linked PRs/plan IDs).
7) If problem is intermittent, capture pcap at node + NAT appliance for at least 5 minutes.

Telemetry & observability (must-haves):
- Metrics:
  - nat.active_connections (per nat_ip, per az/zone)
  - nat.allocated_ips_count and nat.available_ips_count
  - conn_tracking.entries and conn_tracking.failed_allocations
  - dns.query_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99) split by resolver (node-local vs kube-dns)
  - egress.success_rate (per destination prefix)
  - firewall.drop_rate per rule-id
- Logs:
  - NAT appliance logs with conn tracking events and ephemeral port exhaustion warnings
  - Firewall accept/drop logs, include source/dest/port/protocol and policy id
  - Node kube-proxy and iptables/ nft logs when possible
- Traces:
  - Correlate request-id from app logs to network egress path via a sidecar header injected at egress-proxy (if present)

Alerting thresholds (suggested):
- nat.active_connections > 75% of (pool_size * ephemeral_ports_per_ip) over 5m -> P2
- dns.query_latency_p99 > 300ms and error_rate > 1% over 3m -> P2
- firewall.drop_rate > 0.5% of egress flows hitting production routes -> P3
- sudden spike in conn_tracking.failed_allocations -> P1

Terraform module notes (egress-nat module):
- Inputs to standardize across clouds: pool_size, ephemeral_ports_per_ip (defaults: 25600 for cloud-managed NAT), allocation_strategy: [per-zone, centralized], ip_family: [ipv4, dual], tagging_metadata.
- Outputs to export: nat_ips[], nat_gateway_id, route_table_ids, security_group_rules_applied[].
- Backwards-compatible change recommendation: add new variable centralized_gateway { type = string, default = "disabled" } and avoid removing per-zone resources. When enabled, module will create a centralized NAT and attach static IPs; will not destroy existing per-zone NATs unless explicit migrate = true flag set.
- Upgrade plan for module v2 -> v3:
  1. v2 currently names NAT resources as module.<name>.nat_x -> v3 will rename to module.<name>.central_nat_x; sets lifecycle.ignore_changes for nat_ips during first run.
  2. Run terraform plan with var centralized_gateway = "enabled" and migrate = false to create central gateway in parallel.
  3. Switch routing (route table) using a canary AZ: update route in one AZ to point to centralized as a new route with lower priority. Monitor for 30m.
  4. If stable, set migrate = true to decommission per-zone NAT in a controlled apply window.

Common failure modes and remediation steps:
- Symptom: Intermittent 502s and external servers see unexpected source IPs -> likely NAT hairpinning / asymmetric routing.
  - Remediation: Check egress-proxy and ensure SNAT performed only at gateway. Validate iptables MASQUERADE rules are not present on both nodes and gateway.
- Symptom: All egress connections drop after midnight -> conn tracking table overflow due to long-lived idle connections.
  - Remediation: Tune conntrack max (sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max), enable periodic cleanup, recommend app keep-alive timeouts. Add conntracking exporter to dashboard.
- Symptom: DNS resolves internal name to public IP causing egress to wrong region -> split-horizon mismatch after zone transfer/caching.
  - Remediation: Flush resolver caches, confirm stub resolver config, add DNS TTL override in service discovery until authoritative zone is fixed.

Firewall / network policy checklist for Private deployments:
- Restrict host egress to egress-proxy or egress-gateway subnets only. No direct 0.0.0.0/0 from app-subnet.
- Use deny-by-default with explicit allow lists for expected destinations (e.g., registries, telemetry endpoints).
- Apply QoS shaping for telemetry flows to avoid saturation of NAT ephemeral ports by noisy consumers.
- NetworkPolicy for k8s: explicit egress to Cluster Egress IPs and cluster-internal services; label-based policies for critical system namespaces.

Canary / cutover plan (per customer):
- Prework: Inventory per-zone NAT elastic IPs, current ephemeral port usage, and active conn counts.
- Phase 0 (dry-run): Deploy central NAT with new IPs, do not change routing. Validate metrics and logs for 24h.
- Phase 1 (single AZ canary): Update route table for AZ-a to point to central NAT. Keep per-zone NAT for others. Monitor application success_rate, nat metrics, firewall logs for 60m.
- Phase 2 (multi-AZ incremental): Roll AZ by AZ (wait 60m–2h depending on traffic).
- Phase 3 (migration finalize): Once 100% traffic flows through central NAT and stable for 24h, run terraform apply with migrate=true and decommission per-zone NAT resources during maintenance window.
- Rollback: Repoint AZ route back to per-zone NAT and set migrate=false. Terraform destroy will be avoided unless explicit.

Debugging commands & artifact collection (quick copy-paste):
- On node: sudo tcpdump -i any host <dest-ip> and port 443 -w /tmp/egress.pcap
- On NAT: show conntrack | grep <source-ip> or sudo conntrack -L | grep <pod-ip>
- iptables-save | grep MASQUERADE
- Check NAT metrics: curl $METRIC_ENDPOINT/metrics | grep nat.active_connections
- Firewall logs: gcloud logging read "resource.type=... AND protoPayload.methodName=drop" --limit 100

Open questions / decisions to resolve before wide rollout:
- Do we enforce central NAT as default for all new customers, or make it opt-in? (pro: easier observability; con: single-point-of-failure).
- TTL conventions for split-horizon zones during migration windows.
- Standard ephemeral_ports_per_ip value for on-prem NAT boxes (need vendor guidance).

Action items (owners):
- Asha: draft Terraform patch to add "centralized_gateway" var and lifecycle.ignore_changes. (ETA: 2026-02-28)
- Miguel: prototype nat.active_connections exporter for on-prem NAT box (ETA: 2026-03-07)
- Lina: dashboard & alert playbook in Console for customers using centralized egress (ETA: 2026-03-14)
- Rory: write a customer-facing one-pager about differences between per-zone and centralized NAT for Solutions Eng (ETA: 2026-03-04)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider adding ephemeral port reservation per-tenant for multi-tenant on-prem appliances to avoid noisy neighbors.
- Explore using TCP proxy with connection pooling in heavy outbound streaming workloads to reduce port usage.

References and links:
- Terraform module repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/128
- Relevant Jira: JIRA-ENG-NET-317
- Confluence design doc (draft): CONFLUENCE-PLAT-4821

End of runbook.

Status: draft -> in_review. Please add notes inline or ping #private-deployments with any objections to the migration plan.
